title: Request from unknown client — no clients.conf entry for this NAS
plain_english: The packet reached the server, but no client{} entry in clients.conf covers its source IP, so FreeRADIUS silently ignored it. The NAS sees this as a timeout, not a reject — which is why the client device just spins and eventually gives up.

causes.cause: There is simply no client entry for this NAS yet (new AP/switch, or its IP changed).
causes.next_check: Add a client{} block in clients.conf with the exact source IP shown in the debug output, set the shared secret, and restart or HUP radiusd.

causes.cause: The NAS is multi-homed or behind NAT and sends RADIUS from a different interface/IP than the one you whitelisted.
causes.next_check: Compare the source IP in the debug line with what you configured; on the NAS, look for a 'RADIUS source interface' setting and pin it.

causes.cause: The client entry exists but the config was never reloaded, or it sits in a virtual server that isn't listening on this address.
causes.next_check: Restart radiusd (or send SIGHUP) and verify with radiusd -X that the client list printed at startup includes this IP.
